text:
support: :rotating_light: incoming — multiple customers reporting 401/403s for API calls starting ~2026-03-17T06:14:00Z. Tickets are piling; support triage says ~12% of requests failing for a subset of tenants. opening thread to coordinate.
ops-bot: Alert: auth-service.verifier errors >= 5/min for 3 consecutive minutes. Related deploy: credential-fanout 2026-03-17T06:12 canary
mia: Looking at signing-service and verifier logs. Fanout job started at 06:13:41 and pushed a new signing key (kid=ku_9f2). Verifier pods show repeated failures: "unknown key id ku_9f2" — they haven't picked up the new JWKS from the cache.
mia: Quick snippet from verifier log: `2026-03-17T06:15:02Z ERROR token.verify failed kid=ku_9f2 tenant=acme reason="kid not found in jwks cache"`
sanjay: @mia can we pause the fanout job? if the service published a key before all verifiers subscribed we get transient 401s. Pause gives us time to reconcile JWKS propagation.
lucy: +1. Runbooks: pause fanout, roll back signing key publish, clear jwks cache, restart 1 verifier canary.
alex: Customer impact numbers (from edge metrics): acme, beta-co, and gamma-prod have highest error rates. I'll open a support template for impacted tenants with ETA and steps.
anna-oncall: Oncall joining. Assigning roles: @sanjay pause fanout, @mia verify jwks propagation, @alex coordinate support messages.
sanjay: Pausing fanout now: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment credential-fanout --replicas=0` — started at 06:20:12Z. ops-bot should post status when scaling completes.
ops-bot: Action: scaled deployment credential-fanout to 0 replicas (by sanjay) at 2026-03-17T06:20:13Z
mia: Confirmed: fanout paused. Next: reconcile verifier caches. I see redis backfill backlog — a previous migration changed the jwks key namespace from `jwks:v1:` to `jwks:v2:` so verifiers are still reading v1 keys while signer published v2. That explains mismatch.
lucy: Oof. So the signing side wrote v2 namespace while verification side still expects v1. Two options: revert signing key publish to previous kid, or update verifiers to read v2. Rolling verifiers now is risky.
sanjay: Let's revert publish first (fastest). mia, can you set signer to publish the previous active kid (ku_7a) and push a no-op to rotation service? If KMS prevents immediate revert we should fallback to legacy validation.
mia: Reverting to ku_7a via KMS: `redwood-kms set-active-key --service=signing --kid=ku_7a` — attempted at 06:24:05Z, command returned success. However, some tokens already have ku_9f2 in headers; we need verifier to accept both for ~5m.
alex: Support message (short): "We’re investigating an authentication issue affecting API calls for a subset of customers. We’ve paused a credential rollout and expect service restoration within minutes. We will follow up with a postmortem." Posting to affected ticket queue.
mia: To allow dual acceptance, enabling legacy fallback: set `AUTH_ACCEPT_OLD_KEYS=true` on verifier config and restart canary pod: `kubectl -n prod scale statefulset verifier --replicas=1 && kubectl -n prod rollout restart statefulset/verifier --selector=canary=true` — doing canary now.
ops-bot: Canary verifier restarted (pod verifier-2-canary) at 2026-03-17T06:29:40Z
mia: Canary logs show it now accepts tokens with kid=ku_7a and ku_9f2. Error rate for canary tenant dropped to ~1% within 60s. Planning to roll forward to rest of verifier fleet.
lucy: Before full roll, let's clear JWKS cache to force propagation: `redis-cli -h redis-prod --scan --pattern 'jwks:*' | xargs -n1 redis-cli -h redis-prod del` — doing in a staged fashion to avoid thundering herd.
alex: Support update posted at 06:33Z: "We paused a credential rollout and performed a configuration rollback on the auth layer. Some customers may still see intermittent 401s while caches propagate. If you continue to see errors please share request id and timestamp."
anna-oncall: Monitoring metrics — 401 rate across all tenants falling from 12% -> 3% over 8 minutes. Good. Keep rollouts staged and watch latency.
sanjay: Root cause summary so far: migration changed jwks namespace format; fanout pushed new kid before verifiers read new namespace. Fix path: revert publish (done) + enable dual-key acceptance (done) + update verifiers to use v2 namespace and re-run a dry-run fanout to validate.
mia: Planned follow-ups: 1) revert migration change on signing-side schema (hotfix) 2) run a dry-run fanout to a non-prod tenant and validate cache propagation 3) re-enable fanout with rate limit + canary 4) postmortem with timeline and remediation (prevent publish-before-verify check).
lucy: I'll own the postmortem doc and include rollout gating: require N verifier confirmations (kafka offset ack) before marking key active.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated — auth 401 rate reduced to baseline. Fanout remains paused. Incident channel will remain open for 1h for monitoring.
support: Closing loop with customers and marking high-priority tickets for follow-up. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
mia: Adding a short repro for SRE: curl example shows failing case when verifier cache misses new kid:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-with-kid-ku_9f2>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# response: 401 {"error":"invalid_token","reason":"kid not found"}
```
sanjay: Good work. I'll coordinate the graded re-enable: `kubectl scale deployment credential-fanout --replicas=1 --namespace=infra` with a slow ramp -> monitor. Hold until I signal.
anna-oncall: I'll be here to approve re-enable after 30m and verify all error rates are stable. Moving to monitoring state."
